subject: BrightApp launch traffic causing 5xx/429 spikes and timeouts
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@brightapp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Unexpected throttling during our launch ramp (help)

Marissa —

We're seeing sustained 429/5xx errors and a bunch of timeouts in the first 20 minutes of our scheduled feature rollout. Traffic was a planned ramp (5k -> 25k qps over 10m) and we followed the ramp guidance you gave us. The front-end observed many user retries which bubbled up into what looks like a retry storm. Critical flows are failing (checkout and search).

Attached are our client-side request logs and a summary of the timing. Can you confirm whether this is throttling on your side or an issue with our retry/backoff? This is live traffic — we need immediate help. Our launch ops alias is cc'd (launchops@brightapp.com).

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Launch & Growth | BrightApp

Attachments: launch-client-logs-20260310.json (json), customer-observed-errors.png (png)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, evelyn.hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, dylan.brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, vivek.kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@brightapp.com>, launchops@brightapp.com
Date: 2026-03-10T09:20:00Z
Subject: RE: Unexpected throttling during our launch ramp (help)

Team — Elena reports elevated 429/5xx and retry storms during a planned ramp. This is in BrightApp's production launch window (Deal BA-ENTERPRISE-421). Please triage urgently:

- Dylan / infra: Can you check realtime ingress throttles, token rate-limits, and gateway 502/504 traces?
- Vivek / Eng: Any model-side OOMs, queue backpressure, or KV-cache saturation?
- Evelyn / CS & Rishi / AE: Start comms with BrightApp. Offer immediate mitigations and arrange a short warroom call.
- Lauren / Security: Are there any telemetry anomalies that look like malformed requests or abuse?

BrightApp says they followed our ramp guidance (5k -> 25k qps). If they've accidentally retried aggressively, we need to recommend an emergency backoff pattern and consider temporary rate-limiting by customer IP/token to protect platform stability.

I'll pull execs in if we need credit/SLA remediation. Tag updates in this thread.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, evelyn.hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@brightapp.com>, launchops@brightapp.com
Date: 2026-03-10T09:35:00Z
Subject: RE: Unexpected throttling during our launch ramp (help)

Quick findings from the edge / ingress team:

- We see a sharp increase in incoming connections starting 2026-03-10T09:05Z consistent with BrightApp reported ramp.
- Token-level 429s increased ~18x in the first 6 minutes. Simultaneously, several downstream host pools reported 502/504 errors when queue depth exceeded thresholds.
- Logs show a tight retry loop from a small set of IPs (client backoff absent) — many requests with identical request-ids arriving repeatedly. This amplified the effective qps.

Immediate mitigations we applied (09:30Z):
- Enabled temporary soft rate-limit for BrightApp token at 50% of requested peak to stop bursting while we stabilize.
- Deployed stricter connection queue caps on the busiest host pool to prevent cascading backend queue timeouts.

Next steps:
- Collect and share server traces (attaching).
- Suggest customer implement exponential backoff + jitter; provide recommended values.
- Consider short-term dedicated capacity for BrightApp for the rest of the launch window.

Attachments: server-traces-20260310.zip

—Dylan
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: evelyn.hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@brightapp.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T10:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Unexpected throttling during our launch ramp (help)

Thanks Dylan — digging into model runtime traces now. Key notes:

- No OOMs in the model workers themselves, but KV-cache hit-rate dropped dramatically under the burst which increased per-request latency (median latency went from 80ms -> 520ms for the affected route).
- Several host pools hit max concurrency and started returning 502s when queue time exceeded the proxy timeout (we should tighten alerting thresholds).

Immediate engineering mitigations we can/do:
- Increase KV cache allocation for BrightApp token regionally for the next 45 minutes.
- Route BrightApp to a slightly larger instance class for the critical endpoints (hot path) to improve concurrency headroom.
- Push a temporary per-token queue cap with prioritized graceful degradation (route non-critical routes to a slower variant).

We recommend the following to BrightApp (tactically):
- Implement client-side exponential backoff with base=200ms, factor=2, jitter=uniform(0, 100ms), max retries=3.
- Limit parallel requests per browser instance and add client-side circuit breaker on 5xx/429 bursts.

If this recurs we should fast-track a dedicated capacity intake (Redwood Dedicated) — I'll prepare a scoped config and ETA.

—Vivek
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@brightapp.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-10T11:00:00Z
Subject: RE: Unexpected throttling during our launch ramp (help)

Elena — thanks for the quick heads up and for sharing the client logs. We're sorry this interrupted your rollout. The infra team applied a soft cap to stop the retry amplification and engineering is routing critical routes to larger instances as a stop-gap.

What we need from BrightApp now (can you share quickly?):
- Confirm whether you can flip on exponential backoff + jitter within the next 15 minutes for the affected checkout/search endpoints (we can provide a tiny patch or config snippet).
- If you have an internal load balancer, throttle upstream concurrency to avoid multiple parallel requests per user agent.

We'll schedule a 30-minute warroom call at 11:30Z to align on actions and monitor the next ramp step. Marissa / Rishi will coordinate the business comms.

Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@brightapp.com>, launchops@brightapp.com
Date: 2026-03-10T18:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Unexpected throttling during our launch ramp (help) — postmortem & exec summary

Team / BrightApp — final summary and next steps after today's incident and warroom:

Root cause: A planned ramp combined with aggressive client retries produced a retry storm that pushed host pools beyond queue capacity, dropping KV-cache hit-rate and elevating per-request latency. This caused cascading 429/5xx and customer-visible timeouts.

What we did (chronological):
- 09:30Z: Edge team enabled token soft rate-limit and connection queue caps to stop amplification.
- 09:35Z: SREs collected traces; engineering increased KV allocation and routed critical routes to larger instance classes.
- 10:00Z: Customer applied exponential backoff (we provided snippet) and reduced parallel requests per user agent.
- 11:30Z: Warroom confirmed stabilization; subsequent ramp steps used a slower slope and did not recreate the storm.

Impact and asks:
- BrightApp saw a 12% error-rate spike across critical flows for ~22 minutes. We offered a goodwill credit and committed to a joint postmortem and concrete ramp plan.
- Engineering: please produce a short runbook (<=2 pages) for future customer ramps that includes per-token soft-limits, recommended client backoff snippet, and criteria for offering Dedicated capacity. Due: 2026-03-12T17:00Z.
- SRE/Infra: add automated alert when KV-cache hit-rate drops > 40% and when token 429 rate > 5% in 5 minutes. Due: 2026-03-14.
- Sales/CS: Rishi/Evelyn, prepare the customer-facing incident note and the credit terms by EOD tomorrow.

Exec note: I flagged the incident for leadership given revenue impact and exec sensitivity of the launch. No further escalation required at this time but I'll ping if BrightApp requests expanded credits or SLA exceptions.

Attachments provided: loadtest-results-20260310.csv, recommended-ramp-guidance.pdf

Thanks — clean handoff to owners above.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
